findings.section: C21.04-E1 and Boundary to carry forward
findings.defect: The explicit instruction to keep m/m_e symbolic when m_e is absent confuses a dimensionless ratio with the dimensional mass. Once c and the contributing entries of b are supplied, m/m_e=c dot b is numerically determinable without the numerical reference mass. Missing m_e blocks numerical m, not this ratio. The surrounding source-input cautions are valid but do not justify withholding the computable ratio.

counterexample.source: Existing worked toy renderer with the reference-mass value withheld

findings.correction: Replace the incorrect sentence with: 'If a contributing renderer input such as a_e is absent, retain the corresponding symbolic term. If only m_e is absent, report any computable ratio c dot b and retain m=(c dot b)m_e symbolically.' Clarify the line57 boundary the same way, propagate into generated assembly/authoring text, and add an answered missing-reference-mass check using the existing ratio3 example. Refresh audit/manifest/completion and rerun validation.

source_and_authority_boundaries.saturation_proof: The independently checked integer recipes give L_int A=I6. For an integer vector z in im_R(A), z=Ac and c=L_int z is integer, hence z belongs to im_Z(A). For a separately supplied integer rank7 L with LA=0, real equality and this saturation imply ker_Z(L)=im_Z(A). This neither identifies source L nor asserts Aplus y is integer for every integer y.
